title: The Friday reporting scramble
objective: Understand how small agency teams prepare client reports, existing workarounds and their impact.

turns.speaker: cofounder
turns.text: Tell me about your role and how you prepare client reports.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: I run operations at a small marketing agency. Reporting is a headache every week.

turns.speaker: cofounder
turns.text: Can you walk me through the last time you prepared one?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Last Friday I exported numbers from three ad platforms, pasted them into a spreadsheet and checked each total. It took two hours.

turns.speaker: cofounder
turns.text: What happened after you checked the totals?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: One total was wrong. Our account manager caught it before sending the report, but we delayed the client meeting by half an hour.

turns.speaker: cofounder
turns.text: What have you tried to make this easier?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: We bought a dashboard tool for 80 dollars a month. We still use the spreadsheet because two clients want their own format.

turns.speaker: cofounder
turns.text: How often does a report actually delay a meeting?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Only twice this quarter. Most reports are fine. Client onboarding takes more of my time than reporting.

turns.speaker: cofounder
turns.text: Tell me about the most recent client onboarding.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Yesterday I chased four people for account access. We could not start work until the client owner approved it this morning.
